requirements.requirement: - One local Git repository, Node 24.x, npm, root `package.json` and committed `package-lock.json`; Linux and macOS. Pin exact dependency versions at build kickoff and record them in the lockfile and evidence. Other runtime majors are untested initially.
requirements.note: Exact Node/npm/dependency/browser pins exist. C2 passes 221 unit and 95 integration cases on each platform, all 18 installed commands on each platform, and the pinned Linux release gate. Executed platform scope is Node 24.22.2 on macOS arm64 and Linux arm64; other architectures and hosted CI are not claimed. Linux lsof 4.99.7 prerequisite and rejection of 4.95 are verified.

requirements.requirement: - BEFORE defaults to exact `HEAD`; AFTER defaults to a snapshot of the current filesystem (`WORKTREE`). Explicit refs select exact commits. An explicit merge-base option is available.
requirements.note: Default HEAD to WORKTREE, exact divergent endpoints, detached HEAD, merge-base and rename semantics have real Git cases. The C2 installed smoke renders both default saved WORKTREE plans and the actual selected merge base.

requirements.requirement: - Isolated, disposable workspaces and independent dependency installs. No mutation of the caller's source files, index, dependencies, or branch by the tool.
requirements.note: Separate real installs, caller HEAD/index/full-filesystem preservation, copy races and later caller-edit isolation have tests. C2 packed WORKTREE and real-app runs preserve ignored dependencies, modes, empty directories and symlink identities.

requirements.requirement: - A pure planner; basic Next.js App Router route detection; explicit routes and a custom start command for other apps. No claim of complete change coverage.
requirements.note: Conservative routing, custom argv, and explicit selection are implemented. Planning probes stop at consent without execution.

requirements.requirement: - One desktop viewport, 1280×800, DPR 1, Chromium. Up to three sequential scenarios, each up to twelve steps. Both sides advance through the same step indices.
requirements.note: Bounds, shared step indices, fresh scenarios, and actual 1280x800 screenshots have focused evidence.

requirements.requirement: - JSON config and scenarios; exact locators; explicit expected absence; truthful failure/coverage status.
requirements.note: Strict operands and the absence/failure state matrix are covered. C1 path rejection was repaired and independently checked in the 50-case schema gate.

requirements.requirement: - MP4, PNG poster, masked source keyframes, composed keyframes, manifest, and local `pr.md`. No upload.
requirements.note: C2 installed success and partial runs produced every named local artifact. Public-demo copies and all declared artifact/image hashes were independently verified. Pixel continuity covers masked failure frames through decoded media.

requirements.requirement: - CLI, JSON output, a shipped generic agent skill, cleanup, diagnostic `doctor`, and an installed-package smoke test.
requirements.note: C2 clean installed binary passed help, doctor, planning, comparison, re-encoding and strict JSON/error cases. Generic skill and relative references ship. Owned clean behavior has real CLI and ownership tests.

requirements.requirement: MCP, live accessibility snapshots, planner server reuse, asynchronous job registries, editor-specific skill installers, interactive scenario recording, TS/YAML configs or scenarios, import graphs, additional framework adapters, auth profiles, env copying, database hooks, HAR replay, shared-backend mutation support, dependency/worktree caches, reused external servers, continuous/burst video, cursor animation, fuzzy locator fallback, diff boxes, GIF/WebM, multiple devices, monorepos, Windows, native apps, publishing/comment bots and a GitHub composite action.
requirements.note: Deferred scope is absent from exposed flags and schemas. This is a negative-scope source/doc review, not a test of deferred behavior.

requirements.requirement: An MCP adapter may be planned after this release; it must not consume the 24-hour correctness buffer. A CLI plus a skill already serves agents. There is no inference/model call inside the product.
requirements.note: Product source and dependencies contain no model client or MCP adapter. Static inspection supports this scope constraint.

requirements.requirement: A clean install of the packed npm artifact must produce a correct comparison on the synthetic two-commit fixture, including an AFTER-only toggle and a retained hover state. It must also demonstrate a visibly incomplete comparison and exit 3 when a required BEFORE step fails. Repeated runs must leave the original checkout unchanged and no supervised child processes alive.
requirements.note: C2 packed quickstart proves expected BEFORE absence, AFTER-only control, retained hover and required BEFORE partial exit 3. Full source-preservation and process checks pass. Actual decoded success/partial media has manual visual review.

requirements.requirement: Public launch depends on §12 evidence, not on elapsed time. The 24-hour target assumes four concurrent owners, access to Linux CI and macOS, and local prerequisites. If required gates fail, deliver the runnable work with failure evidence; do not describe it as a completed release. This audit does not authorize package publication, external uploads, domain purchases, or repository visibility changes.
requirements.note: All required C2 runtime, package, media, security and requirement gates pass. Concrete owner handoff records exact bytes and remaining publication actions. Publication, uploads, repository visibility changes, credentials and provenance setup remain outside build authorization; elapsed time is not used as acceptance evidence.

requirements.requirement: Use one TypeScript ESM npm package. Build with `tsc`; use `commander`, Zod 4 (including its JSON Schema export), `playwright`, `pixelmatch`, `pngjs`, `semver` (engine checks), and `vitest`. Use Node `child_process.spawn` with argument arrays and `shell:false`. No `jiti`, `sharp`, native canvas, static FFmpeg bundle, router AST parser, or orchestration framework is needed.
requirements.note: Required ESM/tool stack and argument-array process launch are present. No forbidden runtime dependency was found.

requirements.note: CLI owns one-envelope printing, diagnostics, prompt, and operating-system signals.

requirements.requirement: `RunContext` contains run ID, absolute owned directories, a monotonic deadline, cancellation signal, private diagnostic sink, and a resource registry. It also holds a `Supervisor` interface (`spawn`, `stop`, `stopAll`) used by all execution modules. Every process, browser and workspace registers immediately upon creation. A failed module still leaves owned resources reachable by `finally`. Errors are typed and carry stable code, phase, optional side/step ID, sanitized message and next action.
requirements.note: Resource registration and typed failures have real process and browser tests. Independent terminal ownership review matches frozen source hashes. Browser deadline ordering repair has macOS and focused Linux execution evidence.

requirements.requirement: Composer may launch its own isolated Chromium context for rendering the comparison template. It must not receive live recorder pages or depend on the apps staying up. Encoding/re-encoding consumes persisted composed PNGs and a timeline, with no browser required.
requirements.note: Synthetic render is independent of app servers. Fresh process re-encoding succeeds without browser or font assets.

requirements.requirement: Repository layout:
requirements.note: Declared modules, schemas, assets, skill, and documents exist. Installed-package checks use scripts/release-smoke.mjs instead of a test/package directory; this is a location difference, not missing behavior.

requirements.requirement: - All persisted documents have `schemaVersion: 1`; reject unsupported versions. Strict object schemas reject unknown keys. Publish generated schemas in the package; generation must be deterministic and checked in CI.
requirements.note: Strict versioned schemas and deterministic schema:check pass. The installed C2 gate loads all seven shipped JSON schemas and validates documented examples against runtime and generated contracts.

requirements.requirement: - Config, scenario and plan input files are UTF-8 JSON, at most 1 MiB each; parsing never evaluates code. IDs match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}` and are unique within their parent. Scenario IDs are unique within a plan; step IDs are unique within a scenario.
requirements.note: UTF-8/1 MiB, version/ID/uniqueness, and FIFO refusal are directly checked.

requirements.requirement: - No user-supplied ID, ref, caption, filename or URL is interpolated into a shell/filter expression. Generated filenames use numeric indices and fixed suffixes. Paths from imported bundles must be relative, contained regular files; reject absolute paths, `..`, symlinks and missing images before reading them.
requirements.note: Numeric filenames, spawn arrays, imported file containment, symlink rejection, and literal rendering have tests.

requirements.requirement: - Human text is capped at 160 Unicode code points, strips terminal control characters, and is assigned using `textContent` in the renderer. `fill.value` is at most 4096 characters and is never used in captions, logs, or public summaries. It may exist in the private plan; avoid real credentials entirely in this release.
requirements.note: Unicode code-point limits, textContent, secret/fill exclusion, and private plan presence are checked.

requirements.requirement: - Read input paths relative to the invocation directory. Config lookup uses the Git root. All relative paths inside a saved plan or artifact document are relative to its documented root, never the current shell directory.
requirements.note: Inputs resolve from invocationDir; config resolves from Git root; compose succeeds from another directory using run-relative files.

requirements.requirement: - All elapsed timings use Node monotonic time. Wall timestamps are ISO UTC strings. Fractions are finite; timeouts are positive bounded integers; encoded timeline boundaries are integer frames.
requirements.note: Node performance.now deadlines, ISO timestamps, finite values, and integer schedules are implemented and exercised.

requirements.requirement: Every JSON command writes exactly one document to stdout, including on error. No spinner, child log, warning, debug message or newline-delimited progress record shares stdout. Diagnostics go to stderr. Commands without `--json` may format the same result for people.
requirements.note: Success, early error, partial, deadline, phase signals and terminal-write interleavings emit one JSON document. C2 source and installed command checks include the corrected terminal protocol.

requirements.requirement: `status:partial` and exit 3 may include a useful manifest/artifacts. An early failure returns `data:null`. If a run directory exists, write a terminal manifest even when capture/encoding fails. `SIGKILL` and power loss cannot guarantee a terminal write; a subsequent doctor reports an abandoned running state.
requirements.note: Normal partial/error/cancel terminal writes and SIGKILL residue are covered. Independent probes verify cancellation through terminal writes. Persistent write failure returns null data and a warning that saved files may show earlier state.

requirements.requirement: `Plan` contains:
requirements.note: Structural Plan introduction. The following rows map each field and freshness rule.

requirements.requirement: - `schemaVersion`, `planId` (SHA-256 of canonical JSON excluding ID and generated timestamp), `generatedAt`;
requirements.note: calculatePlanId excludes planId/generatedAt and uses canonical SHA-256. Tampered saved plan is rejected in the independent CLI probe.

requirements.requirement: - `repoRoot` (canonical real path; private), `requestedBase`, `requestedHead`, `baseCommit`, `headCommit` (full Git OIDs), `baseResolution: exact|merge-base`, and `headKind: commit|worktree`;
requirements.note: Canonical repo root and pinned full OIDs are used; explicit plans tolerate a different caller HEAD.

requirements.requirement: - `sourceFingerprint` of the current source inventory when WORKTREE is used; `configDigest`; private `configSource: {path:string, rawSha256:string}|null` identifying the selected config file (including custom paths); resolved normalized config and scenarios;
requirements.note: Raw config bytes and parsed config digest share one read. Config newline and WORKTREE mutation invalidate saved plans.

requirements.requirement: - `changedFiles: {status, oldPath: string|null, newPath: string|null}[]` sorted by path;
requirements.note: Exact diff and inventory-diff tests include deletion/addition, sorted paths, and NUL filenames.

requirements.requirement: - `coverage: {selected, unresolved, omitted, unsupported, complete}`; each route candidate has `path`, `reason`, `via` and optional reason for nonselection;
requirements.note: Coverage buckets, reasons, selection order, and explicit coverage limits have table fixtures.

requirements.requirement: - `execution`: command argv arrays, cwd labels, intended install per side, and the network/side-effect notice. Never include environment values;
requirements.note: Preview contains exact argv, side cwd labels, file counts, and privilege/network notice. The real PTY prompt was observed.

requirements.requirement: - `warnings`.
requirements.note: Warnings report explicit/incomplete selection, ignored files, and CSS locators.

requirements.requirement: A saved plan is immutable input. Edit the config/scenario source then regenerate it; do not hand-edit the plan. `compare --plan` checks its ID, schema, repository path, config digest (including the bytes at `configSource.path`, if present) and WORKTREE fingerprint, plus current HEAD equals the pinned `headCommit` only when `headKind` is `worktree`, and fails `STALE_PLAN` (exit 2) on mismatch. Commit refs use the plan's resolved OIDs even if branches subsequently move; tell the user which OIDs are used. Without `--plan`, compare creates the same plan in memory.
requirements.note: Saved-plan ID, source/config identity and WORKTREE freshness checks are implemented. Earlier independent CLI probes cover explicit caller-HEAD movement and tampering. C2 installed smoke exercises exact saved-commit plans, default saved WORKTREE plans and stale WORKTREE rejection. The planner freshness code is unchanged from that focused review.

requirements.requirement: Canonical JSON means recursively lexicographically sorted object keys, array order preserved, UTF-8 JSON without extra whitespace. Source fingerprints follow §5. A plan containing credentials is private input, not a publishable artifact.
requirements.note: Canonical order and digest properties are unit checked; private/public fill separation is integration checked.

requirements.requirement: `CaptureBundle` contains `schemaVersion`, run ID, exact browser/tool versions, capture mode `keyframes`, viewport/DPR, sanitized source labels, and ordered scenarios. Each scenario has its ID/title, ordered steps, and each step has:
requirements.note: Persisted CaptureBundle validation covers versions, labels, ordered states, and actual browser version.

requirements.requirement: There is always a frame for both sides, including when the first navigation fails; use a generated neutral panel until a real safe capture exists. No screenshot taken for diagnostics bypasses the masked capture path. A held frame never has status `ok` for a later failed/blocked step. Do not serialize `fill.value` or full browser error objects into the bundle.
requirements.note: Neutral first failure, held statuses, zero unsafe fallback, and public fill exclusion have direct real-browser cases.

requirements.requirement: `Timeline` contains `schemaVersion`, run ID, `fps:30`, `templateVersion:1`, `width:1920`, `height:686`, `totalFrames` and `segments[]`. A segment has `kind:title|step`, nullable scenario/step IDs, a composed PNG path, `startFrame` and `durationFrames`. Starts are cumulative, durations positive, boundaries half-open; the final endpoint equals totalFrames. Also record selected poster path and the hashes of all composed images. Validate limits and hashes on `compose`.
requirements.note: Cumulative half-open integer timeline, bounds, hash validation, and saved poster selection are covered.

requirements.requirement: Only these commands/flags are in v0.1. Unsupported options fail with exit 2 and a concrete alternative.
requirements.note: Unknown/deferred/misplaced options and conflicts fail with exit 2 and help guidance.

requirements.requirement: | Command | Behavior |
requirements.note: Structural command table header. Command behavior is mapped in the following five rows.

requirements.requirement: | `show-what-changed [compare]` | plan, request execution consent, snapshot, install, capture and compose |
requirements.note: The actual installed C2 pipeline produces expected success, partial, WORKTREE, saved-plan and automatic-incomplete outcomes with matching artifacts.

requirements.requirement: | `show-what-changed plan` | validate, inspect Git and infer routes, write `.show-what-changed/plan.json`; never execute repo code |
requirements.note: Plan persists private owned JSON, performs source inspection only, and reaches no app script.

requirements.requirement: | `show-what-changed compose <runDir>` | re-encode saved composed PNGs/timeline; does not run app code or change capture outcomes |
requirements.note: Browser-free saved-frame re-encoding and partial outcome preservation are independently demonstrated.

requirements.requirement: | `show-what-changed doctor` | read-only diagnosis, compatible browser install command, system FFmpeg/ffprobe capability check |
requirements.note: Doctor launches tool-owned capability probes, performs tiny H.264 encode/probe, and prints a pinned browser setup command.

requirements.requirement: | `show-what-changed clean <runId>` | delete one inactive owned run and its owned workspace residue under §11; refuse active/uncertain ownership |
requirements.note: Exact owned cleanup refuses active and uncertain ownership; SIGKILL recovery and clean/compose races are tested.

requirements.requirement: Common: `--json`, `--help`, `--version`. Compare/plan: `--base <ref>` (HEAD), `--head <ref|WORKTREE>` (WORKTREE), `--merge-base` (off), repeatable `--route <path>`, repeatable `--scenario <file>`, `--config <file>`. Compare alone: `--plan <file>`, `--allow-exec`, `--timeout <seconds>` (600, maximum 3600), `--ci`. `--plan` excludes source/config/scenario/route overrides. `--ci` is also enabled by `CI=true` and never prompts. `--allow-exec` is explicit permission for this invocation, not persistent trust. Agents may use it only with user authorization to run this app's code.
requirements.note: Common/source/execution flag sets, conflicts, timeout bounds, and CI no-consent behavior are covered.

requirements.requirement: `--scenario` and `--route` are mutually exclusive. CLI routes replace configured routes. CLI scenarios replace automatic scenario generation. At most three routes/scenarios; excess explicit input is an error. Auto candidates are capped at three and omissions are reported. Config precedence: built-in defaults → JSON config → CLI, applied once during planning. No environment variable silently grants trust or changes a plan.
requirements.note: Selection precedence and limits are table checked. Config defaults apply once; no environment trust variable exists.

requirements.requirement: Example after installing the pinned release and prerequisites:
requirements.note: Documented arguments parse. C2 installed exact-ref, saved-plan, WORKTREE and actual merge-base comparisons execute successfully. README route-plan and saved-plan commands run on a dirty fixture.

requirements.requirement: First interactive compare shows the two source identities, source file counts, install/start argv, network notice and output location, then asks for consent if `--allow-exec` is absent. Noninteractive execution without that flag exits 7 before creating worktrees, installing or launching. Plan/doctor never need repo-execution consent. Doctor is allowed to run tool-owned Git/version/capability probes with hooks/external diff/fsmonitor disabled; it never invokes app scripts.
requirements.note: Actual PTY preview/deadline, noninteractive refusal before run creation, and installed plan/doctor are recorded.

requirements.requirement: Optional root `show-what-changed.config.json`:
requirements.note: Documented config JSON accepts runtime/generated schemas and nested defaults.

requirements.requirement: The example's dev argv is the automatic Next default; custom apps require an explicit `dev.argv`. Framework enum is `auto|nextjs-app|custom`. `auto` recognizes `next` plus root `app/` or `src/app/` (both is an error); it otherwise needs custom config and explicit routes. No zero-config promise for Vite or arbitrary package scripts.
requirements.note: Custom config requires argv; ambiguous roots reject; unsupported automatic frameworks require explicit custom setup.

requirements.requirement: `dev.argv`: 1–32 string arguments, `{port}` required as its own argument exactly once, no other interpolation. `readyPath` is a validated app-relative path; `readyStatus` is 1–10 exact HTTP status integers, default `[200]`, never an inclusive range. `timeoutMs` is 1000–120000. `fixedTime` is a UTC ISO timestamp or `null` to disable. Masks are at most twenty CSS selector strings. Step timeout is 100–10000 ms; hold is 200–2000 ms. Default route sample map is empty. No env, hooks, arbitrary evaluate, credentials or command strings are part of config.
requirements.note: Field bounds and standalone port placeholder are defined. Lifecycle uses exact status 201 and rejects 204 instead of accepting a range.

requirements.requirement: - Require a nonbare repository with an existing commit and cleanly resolved index; reject unmerged entries, sparse checkouts, submodules, LFS pointers, symlinks and nonregular source files for v0.1. Reject workspaces/monorepos (`workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`), unsupported package managers, missing lockfile, and conflicting lockfiles before execution. Report the file and supported alternative. No automatic fetch, stash, checkout of the caller, reset, or upgrade.
requirements.note: Full preflight identifies safe offending filenames and supported alternatives. Exact built LFS probe passes. Selected-commit symlink/submodule fixtures with whitespace/newlines assert JSON-quoted offending paths. All 60 source cases pass in each final C2 platform suite.

requirements.requirement: - Resolve requested refs once using `git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`; reject ref values beginning `-`. Full OIDs are strings, not assumed 40 characters. Empty/missing refs fail with exit 2.
requirements.note: Dash/missing refs, detached HEAD, shallow missing commit, and full OID resolution are checked.

requirements.requirement: - Without `--merge-base`, render exact resolved BEFORE and AFTER. With it, BEFORE becomes the unique merge base of the requested base commit and the resolved AFTER commit (HEAD for WORKTREE). Zero or multiple merge bases fail with an actionable error. No hidden default-branch lookup.
requirements.note: Real Git fixtures cover unique merge-base selection and zero/multiple rejection. Installed C2 smoke on both platforms renders the actual selected base, verifies source identities and materialized hashes, and checks all three pair ratios are zero.

requirements.requirement: - Commit comparison: `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --name-status -z --no-renames BASE_OID HEAD_OID --`. Rename detection is deliberately disabled; a rename is a deletion plus addition and both paths are considered.
requirements.note: No-renames exact diff is used; the real rename fixture expects deletion plus addition.

requirements.requirement: - WORKTREE comparison: compare the base-tree content/mode inventory directly against the final filesystem inventory in §5.2, including `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z` candidates. Do not use `git diff BASE --` as the authority: its index-mediated behavior can disagree with the rendered snapshot and invoke clean filters. In particular, a file removed only from the index but still present on disk is not deleted in the rendered state, even if newly ignored. The rendered state is final disk contents, not a union of staged and unstaged patch text. A staged edit reverted on disk must not appear as changed content.
requirements.note: Final disk content wins over staged content, retained ignored index-only deletion is present, and absent/new files are explicit.

requirements.requirement: - Parse filenames as NUL-delimited data, sort deterministically, and do not print control characters to a terminal. Ref/path input is always an argument. Disable Git hooks for managed worktree operations and fsmonitor/external diff for inspection. Reject invalid UTF-8 paths in v0.1 instead of corrupting them.
requirements.note: NUL/newline filenames, invalid UTF-8, hook suppression, configured filters, and conditional linked-worktree filter rejection are checked.

requirements.requirement: WORKTREE means a captured filesystem snapshot, not a live checkout server. Hold a tool-level repository run lock during preparation and execution; this prevents another tool run, not an editor, from writing.
requirements.note: Caller edits cannot change copied snapshot bytes. Repository locking serializes tool runs while explicitly allowing editors to write.

requirements.requirement: 1. Enumerate the union of paths tracked by HEAD, paths tracked by the index, and nonignored untracked paths. Exclude `.git/`, `.show-what-changed/`, `node_modules/`, `.next/`, `dist/`, `build/` from tool inputs. If such generated directories are tracked, fail with `UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE_LAYOUT` rather than silently omit tracked source. Ignore ignored untracked files, including typical `.env.local`; print that they are not copied.
requirements.note: Union enumeration, ignored environment files, tracked generated directories, and absent markers are exercised.

requirements.requirement: 2. Validate regular files, modes, path containment, count and byte bounds. Reject file-to-directory or directory-to-file transitions between the pinned checkout and final snapshot as `UNSUPPORTED_SOURCE_LAYOUT` in v0.1; do not attempt an ambiguous overlay. Limit source snapshot to 20,000 files and 200 MiB total. Exceeding limits fails early with the measured count/size and a support limitation.
requirements.note: Exact 20,000-path and 200 MiB inventory boundaries pass. Sparse MAX+1 file now returns SOURCE_LIMIT exit 2 with measured size and bound. Actual aggregate disk overflow reports at least the bytes measured before cutoff, with a later eligible file in the regression. C2 built-module recheck passes.

requirements.requirement: 3. For each path record existence, executable bit, length, SHA-256 of bytes; deletions have an explicit absent marker. Sort by UTF-8 path bytes. Hash this inventory as `sourceFingerprint`. Include index identity separately for the preservation test, not as rendered content.
requirements.note: Fingerprints include existence, executable mode, byte length, and SHA-256 in UTF-8 byte order. Preservation tests compare index bytes separately.

requirements.requirement: 4. After execution consent, create a fresh detached worktree at the plan's pinned `headCommit` in a private owned temporary directory; overlay captured final bytes/modes, delete files absent from disk, and add nonignored untracked regular files. Never follow source or destination symlinks. Ensure all path ancestors remain inside the owned workspace. Use exclusive owned temporary files and atomic rename for copies.
requirements.note: Detached no-checkout materialization and atomic overlay are tested against final bytes, untracked additions, modes, source mutations, and output symlinks.

requirements.requirement: 5. Re-enumerate/re-hash source input immediately after copying. If it differs from the plan/inventory, fail `STALE_SOURCE` (exit 2), clean the incomplete workspace, and ask for a rerun. Do not silently capture a mixture of source revisions. This is best-effort detection of concurrent edits, not a filesystem-wide atomic snapshot guarantee.
requirements.note: Real concurrent copy mutation and change-and-restore races fail STALE_SOURCE and clean owned workspaces.

requirements.requirement: 6. From this point the AFTER app runs only from the owned snapshot. Later edits to the caller do not affect it. Persist the hash of actual snapshot bytes. Require the destination content/mode inventory to match the intended snapshot as well, catching change-and-restore races during copying. Re-enumerate and hash the full eligible source inventory, including new nonignored files, after install and after capture; if they changed, invalidate provenance and return failed exit 5 before capture, or partial exit 3 if media can be produced after capture, never success. Generated ignored build outputs are outside this identity.
requirements.note: Snapshot isolation and newly added materialized source detection pass. The real CLI provenance case creates an AFTER source file during capture, returns partial exit 3 with valid media, and checks caller preservation, hashes and owned-process cleanup.

requirements.requirement: Source fingerprints identify bytes supplied to the app. They do not identify external APIs, database contents, remote fonts, system libraries, environment, or nondeterministic server code. The manifest explicitly records `dataParity: unverified`.
requirements.note: Every manifest declares dataParity unverified. Documentation distinguishes source identity from external data.

requirements.requirement: For each commit side use a separate detached worktree with a unique run/side path, even when both OIDs match. Git hooks are disabled. Local checkout attributes such as line-ending conversion can affect materialized files; custom filters are rejected; compute actual source-file hashes after materialization and record them alongside OIDs. Reject LFS pointer content rather than downloading. Apply the full inventory revalidation before/after install and capture to BOTH sides, including newly created nonignored source files. Do not reuse any prior worktree or symlink the caller's node_modules.
requirements.note: Both sides have unique detached roots, measured materialized hashes, separate dependency trees, and full revalidation. Same-OID fixtures still use two workspaces.

requirements.requirement: Both sides require a compatible root npm lockfile. Run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` independently in each owned side. npm's download cache may be shared; installed trees/build outputs may not. Install scripts are real arbitrary code and are included in consent. Detect `packageManager` if supplied and reject a non-npm value. `engines.node` incompatibility fails before app startup. Missing npm/Chromium/FFmpeg is exit 8, not an install attempt.
requirements.note: Independent npm ci, source-writing install rejection, engines/npm validation, and pre-execution capabilities are implemented. Missing encoder recovery is exercised.

requirements.requirement: Consented app `npm ci` may download app dependencies. The tool never automatically installs or downloads its own prerequisites (npm/tool packages, browser, OS dependencies or FFmpeg). README and doctor give explicit setup commands using the tool's pinned Playwright version. Shipping `playwright` includes the matching installer entry point; never invoke an unqualified latest `npx playwright` to fix a mismatch. Private registries requiring credentials, local file/link dependencies and workspace dependencies are unsupported in v0.1. Inspect both manifests and lockfiles for these conditions before execution. The full preflight examines both selected trees and the WORKTREE candidate inventory, not only changed files. Preflight filter configuration/attributes before any Git operation that could convert working-tree content, including diff/status/checkout. Git checkout filter configuration is rejected in v0.1 (any configured filter driver or `filter=` attribute); do not run smudge/clean commands. Source-materializing worktree creation starts only after that check and consent.
requirements.note: Both endpoint manifests/lockfiles and WORKTREE are inspected before consent. Aliases now distinguish public npm aliases from forbidden sources. Conditional Git filters reject before checkout.

requirements.requirement: Planning reads both endpoint inventories, so a deleted or renamed page is still a candidate. It does not start a server or inspect live DOM. Scenarios are supplied by a person/agent from its app knowledge, or conservatively generated.
requirements.note: Both inventories feed route discovery. Deleted pages and scoped descendants have table fixtures. No browser dependency exists in planning.

requirements.requirement: Next App support: `app/**/page.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,mdx}` and `src/app/**/page.*`; strip route groups `(name)`. Recognize `[id]`, `[...slug]`, `[[...slug]]` only through explicit route samples in `routes.params`. Ignore `route.*` API handlers and `_private` subtrees. Parallel slots `@slot` and intercepting routes are unsupported and reported; do not silently reinterpret them. Decode neither filesystem names nor arbitrary URLs into executable paths.
requirements.note: Groups, dynamic samples, unsupported slots/intercepts, and ignored API/private files have focused fixtures.

requirements.requirement: - Direct page changes map to the corresponding route from either side.
requirements.note: Direct grouped and new/deleted page candidates are selected from the endpoint union.

requirements.requirement: - `layout`, `template`, `loading`, `error`, and `not-found` changes map to descendant page candidates in that subtree.
requirements.note: SCOPED handles all five declared filenames. A layout fixture checks descendant routes from both endpoint trees.

requirements.requirement: - Shared components, styles, global configs, unknown imports or custom frameworks are unresolved unless explicit routes/scenarios are supplied. Do not guess that `/` covers the whole change.
requirements.note: Known page plus unknown component yields unresolved coverage; custom apps require explicit route or scenario.

requirements.requirement: - Explicit CLI scenarios select their initial `goto` route; CLI routes override config includes; config includes override inference. Explicit selection is recorded as such and does not claim exhaustive changed-route coverage.
requirements.note: CLI routes override config includes; explicit scenarios use their first goto and report EXPLICIT_SELECTION.

requirements.requirement: - Automatic route ranking is direct first, scoped descendant second, then ascending normalized route string. Deduplicate first; select at most three. List overflow as `omitted`. Missing dynamic samples go to `unresolved` with a `--route` hint.
requirements.note: Direct-first ranking, route ordering, deduplication, cap omissions, and missing dynamic sample hints are checked.

requirements.requirement: - Removed/new routes have no automatic permission to fail navigation. The caller must supply an appropriate side-specific scenario (for example an AFTER-only `goto` with a neutral BEFORE panel). A 404 is not evidence that a selector was expected absent.
requirements.note: Generated goto does not permit missing pages; excluded first goto yields a neutral panel; navigation status failure remains failure.

requirements.requirement: - `coverage.complete` is true only if every inferred UI candidate is resolved and selected with no unsupported structure; explicit selections set it false with reason `EXPLICIT_SELECTION`. This does not make every explicit run partial: only failures or **automatic** coverage gaps make exit 3. In automatic mode, any nonempty unresolved, omitted or unsupported bucket is a coverage gap; with at least one captured scenario it yields partial, and with none selected it yields exit 2 as below. Describe coverage separately from execution success.
requirements.note: Planner/reducer/presentation cases cover automatic gaps and explicit selection. The C2 installed mixed-coverage run returns partial exit 3 with successful capture, unresolved source and nonzero coverage omissions.

requirements.requirement: - If no changed files and no explicit selection, exit 4 `NOTHING_CHANGED`. If only proven docs/tests-only paths changed, exit 4 `NO_UI_CANDIDATES`. If changes might affect UI but no route is resolved, exit 2 `ROUTE_REQUIRED`. Never describe uncertainty as proof of no visible change.
requirements.note: Table tests distinguish NOTHING_CHANGED, NO_UI_CANDIDATES, and ROUTE_REQUIRED with exact nonzero exit codes.

requirements.requirement: Proven docs/tests-only patterns: `**/*.md` except `.mdx`, `docs/**`, `test/**`, `tests/**`, `**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`. Root/package/build config changes are unresolved, not automatically ignored. Config/scenario files and internal tool output are excluded from UI-change classification. If classification is ambiguous, request an explicit route in the diagnostic.
requirements.note: docsOnly, excluded config/scenario inputs, and internal output exclusions are implemented. Ambiguous shared source remains unresolved.

requirements.requirement: Automatic scenario for a concrete route: `goto` that route, then `scrollBy {y:640}`, then another `scrollBy {y:640}`. Scroll is instant and clamps independently to each page height. Both sides have the same three steps; it is a bounded sample, not whole-page coverage. Interaction changes require a supplied scenario.
requirements.note: Generated sequence is goto and two 640-pixel instant scrolls. Recorder exercises scroll against differing page sizes.

requirements.requirement: Example `pricing.scenario.json`:
requirements.note: Documented scenario grammar and the extended fixture scenario both validate. The packed fixture exercises expected BEFORE absence and hover.

requirements.requirement: A scenario has schemaVersion, ID, title, and 1–12 steps. Its first step must be `goto`; `only` may restrict it for added/deleted routes. Every side starts on a neutral blank page in a fresh browser context. Scenario state is never reused across scenarios. Each step contains `id`, discriminant `op`, the exact operands below, optional `note`, `only:before|after|both` (both default), `allowMissing:Side[]` (empty default), `timeoutMs`, `holdMs`.
requirements.note: First goto, unique step IDs, 1-12 bound, defaults, neutral excluded side, and fresh scenario storage are tested.

requirements.requirement: | Op | Required operands | Meaning |
requirements.note: Structural operation table header. Each of the seven operations is mapped below.

requirements.requirement: | `goto` | `path:string` | navigate to app-relative path using DOMContentLoaded; HTTP status 200–399, transport success and allowed final origin required; same-document case below |
requirements.note: Real navigation covers success, HTTP failure, external redirect, successful clicked-document fragment, and invalid null response.

requirements.requirement: | `click` | `target:Locator` | Playwright click, actionability and strict matching required |
requirements.note: Real click checks exact locator variants, ambiguity, hidden/disabled controls, action timeout, and neighbor-not-clicked assertions.

requirements.requirement: | `fill` | `target:Locator`, `value:string` | replace input contents; value excluded from output text |
requirements.note: Fill changes input and debounce state; the value remains absent from capture, manifest, timeline, and PR text.

requirements.requirement: | `hover` | `target:Locator` | retain hover until an explicit later action moves pointer |
requirements.note: Real hover followed by assertion and screenshot retains the green hover state in persisted pixels.

requirements.requirement: | `scrollBy` | `y:integer`, -1600…1600 | instant `window.scrollBy(0,y)`; no smooth animation |
requirements.note: scrollBy uses a fixed tool evaluation with instant behavior and bounded integer distance.

requirements.requirement: | `expectVisible` | `target:Locator` | wait for exactly one target to become visible; assertions capture a frame too |
requirements.note: Delayed readiness and hidden/ambiguous failure cases prove exact visibility assertion with subsequent masked capture.

requirements.requirement: | `screenshot` | none | capture present state without moving pointer or altering focus |
requirements.note: Screenshot is an explicit no-action branch and preserves pointer/focus. Hover capture is checked in pixels.

requirements.requirement: `Locator` is exactly one of `{role,name?}`, `{label}`, `{text}`, `{testId}`, `{css}`. Role values must be valid Playwright ARIA roles. Text/name/label are literal strings, exact matching; no regex-string magic, XPath, nth, within, fuzzy matching or fallback lists. CSS is allowed with a warning. Ambiguity (more than one match) is a failure. Maximum locator string length is 512 characters.
requirements.note: Strict one-of locator shapes, valid roles, exact matching, CSS warning, and failed ambiguity are covered.

requirements.requirement: App-relative path starts with `/`, is at most 2048 characters, and when resolved against the side's origin must remain on that origin. Reject `//host`, backslashes, credentials, control characters and alternate URL schemes. A `goto` returning no response is successful only for a same-document fragment transition from a previously successful document to the exact requested app-relative URL; any other null response is a navigation failure. All main-frame navigations and redirects must remain on that side's allocated origin. Popups/new pages, downloads, file choosers and dialogs are unsupported: dismiss/close and fail that side's current step. This is a scope check, not network isolation; subresources and app-server traffic may still use the network.
requirements.note: Origin scope, fragments, unsupported events, and navigation errors have browser fixtures. C1 path controls now reject in runtime/generated schemas; independent 50-case schema gate passed.

requirements.requirement: `allowMissing` is legal only on locator operations and only applies to sides included by `only`. It permits zero matches after bounded locator presence polling; it never excuses ambiguity, disabled controls, hidden existing elements, assertion failure, application crash or a timeout after the element was found. `only` exclusion occurs immediately with no lookup. A required failure blocks every later step on that side of that scenario. The other side continues, and a new scenario gets fresh contexts.
requirements.note: Zero-match allowance, excluded sides, hidden/disabled/ambiguous targets, block propagation, peer continuation, and fresh scenarios have cases.

requirements.requirement: | Condition on a side | Status | Picture | Run effect |
requirements.note: Structural state table header. The five state rows are each mapped below.

requirements.requirement: | operation succeeds | `ok` | new masked capture | none |
requirements.note: Successful operation settles and persists a new masked PNG with no heldFromStepId.

requirements.requirement: | side excluded by `only` | `skipped_by_side` | last safe frame or neutral panel, clear label | expected; not a verified pair |
requirements.note: Immediate exclusion uses safe/neutral frame and visible status; its metric is null.

requirements.requirement: | zero matches and allowed | `expected_absent` | last safe frame, "Expected absent in BEFORE/AFTER" | expected; not a verified pair |
requirements.note: Bounded zero-match expected absence holds safe frame, labels the side, and excludes it from verified metrics.

requirements.requirement: | required missing, ambiguous, unready, assertion/nav error | `failed` | safe failure capture if possible, otherwise last safe frame | partial, exit 3 |
requirements.note: Required side failure produces failure/held pixels, visible incomplete badges, and partial exit 3.

requirements.requirement: | previous required failure | `blocked` | held safe frame, "Not executed after step …" | partial, exit 3 |
requirements.note: Later failed-side steps are blocked. Caption names the actual failed action independently from the last held image.

requirements.requirement: Source `changeRatio` is computed only for `ok/ok` pairs of equal dimensions. Every other pair has `null`; it cannot increase counts of verified unchanged steps. Each scenario outcome is `ok|partial`; the reducer in §10 defines the run status.
requirements.note: Only ok/ok pairs receive pixel ratios. Null states never count as unchanged verified pairs.

requirements.requirement: Launch one pinned Chromium process with two fresh contexts per scenario; viewport 1280×800, DPR 1, locale en-US, timezone UTC, light scheme, reduced motion, service workers blocked. Keep sandbox defaults; do not add `--no-sandbox`. Use no saved auth state, extensions, browser profile or trace recording.
requirements.note: Context settings and explicit chromiumSandbox:true are in code. Real browser storage reset, frame dimensions, and process lifecycle are tested.

requirements.requirement: For each step, execute both eligible sides concurrently, await both terminal results, then proceed. There is no cross-scenario concurrency. Capture exactly one masked keyframe after settlement. No arbitrary scenario JS, app evaluation beyond the tool's fixed scroll/settle logic, CDP capture, HAR or native recording.
requirements.note: Promise.all joins the two step sides before the next step. Fresh sequential scenarios and exact saved frame count are asserted.

requirements.requirement: - Use `page.clock.setFixedTime` before navigation when configured. It fixes browser wall-clock Date while real timers continue; do not pause `requestAnimationFrame`. Use Node time for elapsed measurements.
requirements.note: The real fixture confirms fixed Date, live animation frames, and debounce completion.

requirements.requirement: - Do not replace `crypto.randomUUID`, `crypto.getRandomValues` or server randomness. Seeded Math.random is deferred. Rendered randomness/server dates remain a documented source of noise.
requirements.note: Static inspection finds no random API replacement. Real crypto values appear in the browser fixture; docs disclose randomness noise.

requirements.requirement: - Disable transitions/animations via the tool's own style and screenshot options, hide caret, and force instant scroll. Changes to animations are outside this release's evidence claims.
requirements.note: Shared capture style disables animations/transitions, screenshot hides caret, and fixed scroll is instant.

requirements.requirement: - After each action/assertion, wait for `document.fonts.ready` and two animation frames within the same whole-step deadline. Failed settlement is a step failure, not silently accepted. No network-idle wait. For delayed data the scenario must use `expectVisible` for the relevant ready state.
requirements.note: Real continuous polling does not prevent settled capture; explicit readiness passes; pending font settlement times out as failure.

requirements.requirement: - Fixed time and fresh contexts do not ensure backend/data equality. v0.1 scenarios must use read-only or disposable app data. A click can mutate a backend; the tool cannot infer that it is safe.
requirements.note: Consent/docs require disposable or read-only data. Manifest unconditionally records dataParity unverified.

requirements.requirement: - Every image is captured through one helper with all `maskSelectors`, a solid mask color, viewport-only dimensions and caret/animation settings. Invalid CSS fails before capture; absent selectors are allowed. This is opt-in region masking, not automatic PII detection or blur. Do not persist an unmasked image as a fallback.
requirements.note: Invalid CSS yields no raw fallback. Sentinel privacy is checked in source/failure/composed PNGs and every decoded app frame.

requirements.requirement: - Do not park the pointer before screenshots/checks. A hover followed by a screenshot must retain the hover. Pointer annotations are deferred.
requirements.note: Hover persists through assertion and screenshot; no pointer parking or annotations exist.

requirements.requirement: - Never hide runtime/compiler error overlays to make a capture look healthy. Page errors, navigation failures and server exit fail the affected side. Console warnings are bounded diagnostics and do not by themselves fail the run. Error overlays detectable in the supported fixture fail it; arbitrary application error UI requires an explicit assertion.
requirements.note: Page error, supported overlay, server exit, navigation failures, and late fault before peer completion fail that side. Console warnings stay bounded diagnostics.

requirements.requirement: Whole-step timeout includes locator polling, action, settlement and screenshot. If Playwright has no cancellation API for an active operation, timeout/cancellation closes that context to break it and holds the last safe frame. Do not leave a timed-out action running in the background and start a later step.
requirements.note: Timeout closes context and waits for pending action to settle. Whole-run cancellation keeps typed exit codes.

requirements.requirement: Render a fixed trusted HTML template in a separate Chromium context (no live app DOM). Its only variable inputs are already masked PNG data URLs and sanitized text through `textContent`. Bundle the OFL font and its license, embed the font locally, block all network requests, disable animations and wait for font/image decoding before screenshot. Never insert input as HTML, CSS, script, URL navigation or remote font references. Limit each PNG to 16 MiB compressed, accept only the declared 1280×800 source or 1920×686 composed dimensions as appropriate, and reject unexpected decoded sizes before rendering or encoding. Renderer context has DPR 1, no application storage/init scripts/clock overrides, and a restrictive CSP allowing only its own inline style and PNG/font data URLs. Embed the font as a data URL, so network blocking does not prevent it loading. A missing asset or failed image decode fails rendering; raw masked frames remain available.
requirements.note: Actual isolated renderer checks dimensions, 16 MiB bounds, PNG structure, local font, CSP/network blocking, textContent injection, decoding, and missing assets.

requirements.requirement: Canvas is always 1920×686. Each source viewport is letterboxed without cropping or stretching into a fixed 958×598 panel using `object-fit: contain`; a 4 px divider occupies the center, a 48 px label row is above, and a 40 px caption row below. Labels include BEFORE/AFTER and shortened source identity. No output upscaling or alternate layout is exposed. Status badges/panels are visible in the affected half; capture/coverage/provenance incompleteness known before rendering must be visibly marked in the scenario/run title and captions. Normalize line breaks to spaces. Text uses one line with deterministic ellipsis within measured bounds; never cover the source image to fit long labels.
requirements.note: Pixel geometry verifies 1920x686 with 958x598 halves, divider, letterboxing, titles, status badges, and deterministic ellipsis.

requirements.requirement: Persist one composed PNG per step and one title PNG per scenario. Title cards name the scenario, initial route, capture mode and execution/coverage caveats. A title exists even for the first scenario. The initial release guarantees English labels/captions; preserve Unicode source names in JSON, but map caption/label characters outside printable ASCII to `?` and add `FONT_GLYPH_UNSUPPORTED` rather than claiming multilingual font coverage. This applies only to presentation text, never the app screenshots or saved Unicode JSON; no runtime font-glyph parser is needed. Pin template version `1` in the timeline. All artifacts visibly communicate that these are keyframes; visually incomplete capture cannot appear as a full verified comparison. A cleanup-only failure discovered after encoding is an operational partial, reported in the final manifest, CLI result and pr.md without retroactively claiming the pictures are invalid. The poster uses the same layout and status policy.
requirements.note: Each scenario gets a title; Unicode fallback warning preserves JSON; incomplete poster/captions and cleanup-only operational partial are covered at module boundaries.

requirements.requirement: At FPS=30, each step duration is `ceil(holdMs * 30 / 1000)` frames; default 24 frames (800 ms). Every scenario title is exactly 30 frames. Runtime elapsed milliseconds do not affect presentation length. TotalFrames is the sum once, with no repeated floating-point rounding. Maximum output is three scenarios × (1 second title + twelve × 2 seconds hold) = 75 seconds.
requirements.note: Ceiling holds include 201, 333, 801, and 1999 ms; cumulative frames and full 2250-frame bound are asserted.

requirements.requirement: The encoder uses persisted composed PNGs and an explicit integer-frame schedule. It must produce exactly TotalFrames; image-concat last-frame behavior must be covered by a test. Stream complete composed PNG bytes to FFmpeg `image2pipe` at input framerate 30, repeating each PNG exactly `durationFrames` times in segment order, and set the output frame limit to TotalFrames. Respect stdin backpressure, keep only the current image buffer in memory, close stdin after the final frame, and drain stderr concurrently. This avoids ffconcat duration and final-image ambiguity. No text or pixel-diff computation is performed inside FFmpeg.
requirements.note: Real image2pipe output has exact decoded count and first/boundary/midpoint/final frames. Code awaits stdin backpressure and holds one source buffer.

requirements.requirement: Encode H.264 (`libx264`), yuv420p, CFR 30, CRF 23, preset veryfast, faststart, no audio. Use system FFmpeg and matching ffprobe; explicit executable paths are allowed only through doctor-validated CLI environment `SWC_FFMPEG`/`SWC_FFPROBE`, not from repository config. Command arguments are arrays; do not require drawtext/libass/hstack. Doctor performs a tiny temporary encode/probe, not just `--version`. Capability checks are command-specific: compare needs browser/font plus FFmpeg/ffprobe; encode-only compose needs only validated inputs and FFmpeg/ffprobe, never Chromium/font installation. Doctor reports capabilities independently. Missing required capabilities exit 8.
requirements.note: H.264/yuv420p/CFR/CRF/preset/faststart/no-audio flags are fixed. Actual capability probe, override rejection, and browser/font-free encode pass focused checks.

requirements.requirement: ffprobe validates dimensions, codec, pixel format, rational FPS, decoded frame count and duration within one frame. Extraction tests verify first, transition-adjacent, midpoint and final frames. File size is reported; no promised GitHub upload-size guarantee and no automatic quality-degrading retry. Re-encoding is atomic: use a temporary output, validate, then rename.
requirements.note: ffprobe validates required media properties; extraction checks schedule and lossy tolerance; failed encode retains prior media before atomic rename.

requirements.requirement: The recorder owns computing and persisting changeRatio in CaptureBundle; the composer reads it without mutating the bundle. Use pixelmatch on masked source PNGs before labels/status overlays/resizing, threshold 0.1 and anti-alias differences excluded. `changeRatio = differingPixels/(1280*800)`; it is a visual-difference statistic, not regression correctness or semantic equivalence. `visuallyUnchanged` means ratio <0.001. Noise may count as change. No SSIM, connected-component boxes or DOM diff in v0.1.
requirements.note: pixelmatch runs on masked 1280x800 source frames with threshold 0.1 and includeAA false. Composer preserves ratios. Changed-pair threshold is 0.001.

requirements.requirement: Choose the first step with the highest valid changeRatio as the poster; ties retain scenario/step order. If no valid pair exists, use the first composed step with an incomplete badge. Copy that composed PNG to poster.png. Poster has no hard compressed-byte guarantee.
requirements.note: First maximum wins ties; invalid-pair fallback picks first incomplete composed step; poster is copied from composed PNG.

requirements.requirement: `compose <runDir>` validates the saved timeline and composed-image hashes, then re-encodes MP4 and restores the poster. It needs neither app servers nor Chromium. It cannot change layout/captions/settings or rerun steps. Persist `comparisonOutcome` (capture, coverage and provenance), `cleanupOutcome` and `encodingOutcome` independently in manifest metadata before encoding. A successful compose atomically updates media and its hashes/sizes/paths, current encoding-tool versions and encodingOutcome, recomputes terminal status from preserved comparison/cleanup outcomes, and refreshes pr.md/result; retain old errors in a separate history if useful. It preserves comparison outcomes; it may replace a previous encoding error with success, but cannot repair a failed browser action or invalid provenance.
requirements.note: Recompose validates timeline/image hashes, preserves comparison/cleanup, refreshes media/PR metadata, and recovers encode error without clearing partial capture.

requirements.requirement: Create run IDs as UTC milliseconds plus 8 random bytes, using an exclusive mkdir. The run directory is `.show-what-changed/runs/<runId>/` at the Git root, mode 0700 where supported. Before any plan, run, lock or artifact write, validate canonical containment and reject symlinks or non-directory ancestors in the output root or its managed parent chain; never replace an existing file not registered to this run. Create output files as private (0600) by default. Tool output never participates in source fingerprints or route inference. Do not edit `.gitignore` automatically; tell the user to ignore `.show-what-changed/` before committing.
requirements.note: Exclusive randomized run paths, private modes, canonical managed ancestors, and registered replacement checks are exercised. No gitignore mutation occurs.

requirements.requirement: Manifest contains schemaVersion, tool version, runId, state/status/exitCode, captureMode, start/end timestamps, requested/resolved source identities and materialized hashes (no absolute repo path), browser/Node/FFmpeg versions, config/scenario digests, viewport, dataParity, coverage, per-scenario/per-step statuses, timeline summary, relative artifact paths, artifacts' SHA-256/byte sizes, warnings/errors, phase timings and cleanup result. Missing artifacts are `null`, never nonexistent advertised paths. No fill values, secrets, whole environment, absolute usernames, raw HTTP headers/bodies or full app URLs belong in it. Sanitize diagnostics before including them.
requirements.note: Declared manifest fields, artifact hashes and public privacy have real-run checks. Independent transient/persistent write-failure review verifies truthful terminal results, with null data and explicit warning when public writes cannot commit.

requirements.requirement: Run state transitions:
requirements.note: State transitions are persisted by enter/finally/finalize. Real signal tests observe preparation, startup, recording, and encoding phases.

requirements.requirement: Status reduction after cleanup:
requirements.note: Structural status-table introduction/header. Each status condition is mapped individually below.

requirements.requirement: | Condition | Result / exit |
requirements.note: Structural status-table introduction/header. Each status condition is mapped individually below.

requirements.requirement: | expected steps only, media valid, provenance valid, automatic coverage complete or explicit bounded selection | `ok` / 0 |
requirements.note: Expected absence/exclusion and explicit bounded selection produce success only after valid media/provenance/cleanup.

requirements.requirement: | valid media but any required failure/blocked side, automatic coverage gap (unresolved/omitted/unsupported), source provenance mutation, or cleanup failure | `partial` / 3 |
requirements.note: Actual package runs verify required-step and automatic mixed-coverage partial results. Real CLI source-mutation integration verifies post-capture invalid provenance with valid partial media. Cleanup-only partial has reducer and finalization coverage.

requirements.requirement: | no changes/candidates as narrowly defined in §6 | `nothing` / 4 |
requirements.note: No-change and docs/test-only cases return ToolFailure exit 4 and become status nothing. Final CLI envelope uses the common printer.

requirements.requirement: | input/schema/ref/stale plan/unresolved route/unsupported repository | `failed` / 2 |
requirements.note: Invalid refs/schema/args/layout/inputs and stale config/worktree plans have focused or CLI evidence.

requirements.requirement: | execution consent missing | `failed` / 7 |
requirements.note: Noninteractive missing consent returns exit 7 before workspace/installation/server creation.

requirements.requirement: | workspace or install fails | `failed` / 5 |
requirements.note: Scoped materialization wrapper maps native filesystem failures and failed worktree mutations to exit 5. Sixteen real CLI failure-injection cases and eight snapshot cases pass in each C2 source suite with caller preservation, returned/saved manifest agreement and cleanup. Inspection, missing capability, programmer defect and cancellation codes remain distinct. These are controlled failures, not actual disk-exhaustion tests.

requirements.requirement: | server cannot start/become ready or exits before capture | `failed` / 6 |
requirements.note: Wrong readiness status, timeout/fallback, external redirect, wildcard binding, and early server exit assert exit 6.

requirements.requirement: | missing environment capability | `failed` / 8 |
requirements.note: Unavailable encoder/browser/font paths produce typed capability errors, with actual encode probe used for media capability.

requirements.requirement: | rendering/encoding/output validation fails | `failed` / 9 |
requirements.note: Invalid PNG/hash/timeline and failed encoding map to exit 9. Real terminal-write failure tests preserve earlier fatal/cancel precedence and expose OUTPUT_WRITE_FAILED without claiming uncommitted metadata is saved.

requirements.requirement: | overall timeout | `cancelled` / 10 |
requirements.note: Global deadline passes real CLI/PTY and recorder cases with cancellation exit 10 and cleanup.

requirements.requirement: | SIGINT / SIGTERM | `cancelled` / 130 or 143 |
requirements.note: All eight phase/signal cells run in the complete source suite. Independent late-signal probes and ten terminal-cancellation regressions cover terminal writes, lock release, failed release and invalid-run cancellation.

requirements.requirement: | unexpected internal defect | `failed` / 1 |
requirements.note: normalizeFailure maps untyped unexpected defects to INTERNAL_ERROR exit 1. No deliberate full-CLI unexpected-defect injection was found.

requirements.requirement: Fatal errors take precedence over partial outcome. Cancellation takes precedence if it arrives before terminal result; retain prior failures in errors[]. If cleanup also fails, append it without overwriting an earlier fatal/cancel code. A cleanup error after otherwise successful media is partial. A server exit during recording fails that side, blocks its remaining steps, then composition may produce partial media. `summary` counts verified pairs, visually changed verified pairs, expected absences/exclusions, failed/blocked steps and coverage omissions separately.
requirements.note: Reducers preserve fatal/cancel precedence and distinct counts. Independent real-signal finalization probes now pass for transient and persistent writes and release interleavings. Persistent failure returns null data, truthful warning, and retained ownership.

requirements.requirement: `pr.md` is local preparation: a short summary, local poster/video paths and instructions to attach reviewed artifacts manually. Local paths are not presented as playable remote URLs. No placeholder is advertised as a completed upload. Do not claim compatibility with another skill unless tested against a documented version.
requirements.note: PR text contains local reviewed artifact paths, counts, keyframe/data caveats, and manual attachment instructions. No upload success is claimed.

requirements.requirement: Permission to run repository code is not a sandbox. npm install scripts, dev commands and the application can read local files/network under the user's account. The tool promises **no tool telemetry and no automatic artifact upload**. It does not promise no egress. Page content/scenarios are untrusted data, never instructions to change consent or run shell commands.
requirements.note: Privilege/network warning and no telemetry/upload scope are documented. Code has no uploader/model client. App execution remains an explicit consent boundary.

requirements.requirement: Per-run consent covers the two resolved source identities and exact command argv shown in the plan. No persistent trust file, `--yes`, or `SWC_TRUST` is shipped. Never import executable config during discovery. CI must pass `--allow-exec` deliberately; examples use ephemeral hosted runners, read-only repository permissions, no credentials/secrets, no privileged cache, and never execute fork code in a privileged `pull_request_target` job.
requirements.note: Per-run consent, JSON-only inputs, and unsupported --yes are covered. CI workflow uses read-only permissions, no retained checkout credentials, no pull_request_target, and explicit fixture consent. No hosted run is claimed.

requirements.requirement: Build process environments from an allowlist: PATH, HOME, TMPDIR, platform temp variables, LANG, LC_ALL, plus CI and tool-set PORT, SWC_SIDE, SWC_RUN_ID, BROWSER=none, NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1. Do not propagate arbitrary parent tokens. HOME is not isolation: tools may still read user configuration/credentials; document this. Private diagnostic logs are size-capped to 5 MiB per process; summarize truncation. Redaction of known token patterns/values is defense in depth, not a guarantee; do not print raw child log tails to stdout or package private logs for sharing.
requirements.note: Real process tests verify parent-token exclusion, output drain, 5 MiB cap/truncation, and unrelated-process survival. HOME exposure is documented.

requirements.requirement: Allocate two candidate loopback ports from 4310–4399; exclude duplicates. Port probing has a race, so check that no listener appeared immediately before spawn. Start each command in an owned process group, set assigned PORT and argv placeholder. Never accept silent fallback to another port. Next default binds 127.0.0.1 explicitly. For custom commands document their obligation to honor the exact port and loopback binding.
requirements.note: Distinct candidate ports and exact argv/PORT are checked with real listeners. Bind-after-allocation race retries and preserves unrelated listener.

requirements.requirement: Poll readyPath every 250 ms within the server/overall deadline; each HTTP attempt times out after 1 second and does not follow external-origin redirects. Require an exact configured status and a still-live owned process. Require system `lsof` and `ps` (doctor checks these before execution). Use machine-readable lsof/ps output. Inspect every LISTEN socket on the assigned port: each listener PID must have the live spawned process-group ID and bind only to loopback, never wildcard/nonloopback addresses. Check listener ownership to the spawned process group before accepting readiness; if ownership cannot be established, fail with a diagnostic rather than recording an unrelated service. Next's development port-conflict exit is not treated as readiness. A race retries with a new pair at most twice, only after stopping owned processes.
requirements.note: Machine-readable ownership, loopback-only sockets, exact status, external redirect rejection, fallback/early-exit failure, and conflict retry are exercised.

requirements.requirement: No automatic warm-up of every route: default readiness GET is the only pre-scenario navigation and must be safe. It can compile the app. Actual route readiness is proven by scenario navigation and assertions. Server start timeout is per side but bounded by the global run deadline. Either side's startup failure terminates both sides.
requirements.note: Only configured readiness URL is polled before scenarios; per-side timeout is globally bounded and startup failure stops both sides.

requirements.requirement: The supervisor owns install, start, browser, render and FFmpeg processes, not just dev servers. On success, failure or signal, stop new work, close contexts/browser, send TERM to owned process groups, wait up to 3 seconds, then KILL survivors. Bound total cleanup to 10 seconds. Idempotent cleanup runs once and may be called again safely. Persist cleanup success/errors.
requirements.note: Install/server/browser/FFmpeg groups are owned. TERM then KILL, bounded cleanup, repeated cleanup, and actual phase signals have focused evidence.

requirements.requirement: A repository lock is acquired atomically using an owned lock directory; a second run returns `RUN_ACTIVE` exit 2. Never reclaim a lock or kill a process merely because a persisted PID exists or is absent: PIDs are reusable. During the process lifetime use the live child handle plus group identity. After a crash, doctor lists stale owned paths and possible processes; it never automatically kills them. The user may stop a process manually, then use clean. Lock recovery requires verifying the original owner is gone and no owned workspace is active; uncertain cases fail safely.
requirements.note: Duplicate/stale/incomplete ownership and clean/compose contention refuse unsafe reclamation. SIGKILL diagnosis/registered recovery is checked.

requirements.requirement: `clean <runId>` operates only on an exact registered tool-owned run/temp workspace, validates its ownership marker and canonical containment, refuses symlink roots and active processes, and never uses Git global prune, arbitrary recursive paths, or an all-repos cleanup. Normal cleanup removes private temporary workspaces using their exact registered Git worktree paths and removes the run lock; it retains media/metadata. Never delete the caller's files or node_modules. No automatic age/count pruning in v0.1. SIGKILL/power failure may leave files; disclose that and support manual recovery.
requirements.note: Exact registered cleanup, traversal/symlink/active refusal, failed removal, and SIGKILL recovery preserve caller dependencies and avoid global pruning.

requirements.requirement: The matrix below is required evidence, not a list of tests that have run. Each test has a deterministic fixture; no live paid provider, real user account or production database is a prerequisite. Fixture repositories are created under temporary directories with local Git identity and tagged commits, not checked-in `.git` directories. Pin Linux browser image/tool versions; macOS uses the same Playwright package and browser revision. Cross-platform pixel equality is not required.
requirements.note: Fixtures use disposable locally initialized Git histories and pinned tools. Both final C2 source suites and installed-package gates pass. Linux runs as UID 1001 with Chromium sandbox enabled, pinned Playwright 1.64.1 and Chromium revision 1248. Cross-platform pixel equality is neither required nor claimed.

Include MIT text for authored code, OFL notice for font, notices for any copied code and documented provenance of dependencies. Check exact dependency licenses; an MIT project label does not relicense third-party assets.

Exact quickstart/README commands execute through the installed binary. Final synthetic demo files match their manifests and visual review. Exact dependency-license inventory is recorded.

requirements.requirement: Before public release, scan staged files and complete Git history for secrets, inspect tarball contents, run a dependency advisory audit and triage runtime vulnerabilities. Record npm name availability/owner, repository location and publish credentials as release prerequisites; old availability checks are not reservations. No need to buy a domain or publish a placeholder package. Do not assert trademark clearance or unique market position from absence of registry matches.

Exact-lockfile all/runtime advisory queries report zero vulnerabilities. Registry name availability and unauthenticated publishing identity remain time-scoped owner prerequisites.
